# Model 2

> Model 2 estimates the hidden state of thousands of businesses (capacity, order book, costs, prices) from
> scattered public data, month by month, and forecasts them a year ahead with 90% ranges. It is tested on
> synthetic worlds, where the true values are known. This file tells AI agents how to read the site.

## For agents

- MCP server: https://mikecafarella--model2-mcp.us-east.modal.run/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no key or sign-in). Tools: site_guide, list_forecasts,
  read_page, get_forecast, get_fitted_parameters, get_sector_series, get_official_statistic, search_entities,
  get_entity, search_observations, get_evaluation, get_next_version, get_data_model, get_data_file; and
  send_feedback, the only one that writes: a note for the Model 2 team about anything on the site, tied to its
  forecast, kind, id and month, from a person signed in with Google: it needs the person's feedback key (made on
  the AI Access page, set in the connector). Send feedback only when the person asks you to, in their words.
- Without MCP: every page's text is a Markdown file (below), and every number is in JSON files you can fetch.
- How to connect, client by client: https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/ai.html
- Everything is scoped to one forecast. A forecast determines its world, model and parameter fit. Next Version
  pages are written by AI agents and are not human-reviewed.

## Vocabulary

- World: everything the model may know: entities (businesses), observations (dated public readings) and a sector
  input bundle per as-of date (drivers and official sector statistics). Synthetic worlds are simulated, so their true
  hidden values are known; real worlds are built from public data.
- Forecast: one run of the model on a world, made as of an as-of date (it sees only data published by then), using one
  parameter fit. A forecast determines its world, model and fit. Ids are UUIDs.
- History / nowcast / forecast: months up to the last observed one, from then to the as-of date, and a year beyond.
- Bands: 90% ranges from 100 simulated copies of the world.
- Hit rate: how many of every 100 checked values fall inside the 90% range (about 90 is right).
- Spread ratio: spread of the copies with data over spread without; near 0 the data pin a quantity down, 0.8-1.2 it
  comes mostly from the model, above 1.2 the estimation looks unsettled.
- Next Version pages are written by AI agents and are not human-reviewed.

The site's list of forecasts is https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets.json.

- 976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3 (default): computed 2026-11-13, as of 2026-09-30, covers 2018-10 to 2027-09, world fa0bb576-6164-5022-8c81-57f6bc8908de (synthetic, w34-units-seed20261112); data under https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/

## Pages (text of the default forecast's pages; other forecasts: the same path under their data folder)

- [Overview › Introduction](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/index.md): What Model 2 is and why.
- [Overview › How It Works](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/howitworks.md): The stages: manage worlds and forecasts, build a world, run it forward, score, improve.
- [Overview › Data Model](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/datamodel.md): Every data table, its columns, keys and joins.
- [Overview › Model Structure](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/forecast_model.md): The equations, drawn per kind of business, and the parameters.
- [World Inputs › Introduction](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/world_overview.md): What a world is, its kinds of input, synthetic against real; this world's facts.
- [World Inputs › Entities](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/world_entities.md): The businesses in this world, tracked and representative.
- [World Inputs › Observations](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/world_observations.md): Every published reading, by kind, source and subject.
- [World Inputs › Sector input bundle](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/world_bundle.md): Each sector's drivers and official statistics, as draws.
- [World Inputs › Model Configuration](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/forecast_config.md): Fixed values and starting ranges for the learned parameters.
- [Model and Forecast › Introduction](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/forecast_overview.md): This forecast and the parameter fit it uses.
- [Model and Forecast › Fitted Parameters](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/forecast_fit.md): Each sector's fitted parameters (and ground truth on a synthetic world).
- [Model and Forecast › Forecasts](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/sector.md): Sector totals and entities over time, with 90% bands; ?s=SECTOR, entity.html?e=ID.
- [Evaluation › Forecasts against later estimates](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/eval_revisions.md): How far forecasts moved once later data came in.
- [Evaluation › Observations against the model](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/eval_observations.md): Each observation against the model's prediction.
- [Evaluation › Sector totals against official statistics](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/eval_official.md): The model's totals against official series.
- [Evaluation › What the data pin down](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/evaluation.md): Which quantities and parameters the data determine.
- [Evaluation › Against ground truth](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/accuracy.md): Errors against the true values (synthetic worlds only).
- [Next Version › Current Problems](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/next_problems.md): An AI evaluator's analysis of what is wrong.
- [Next Version › Possible Improvements](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/next_improvements.md): Proposed fixes, with odds, time and cost.
- [Next Version › Improvement Testing](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/next_testing.md): Every possible fix and what testing it found.
- [AI Access › AI Access](https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/pages/ai.md): How AI agents connect to this site (MCP, llms.txt).

## Data files (under a forecast's data folder, e.g. https://mitdbg.github.io/model-2-nowcasting/data/sets/976debf3-7f2a-5e1a-aec0-e24ae8ea99d3/)

- `meta.json`: the forecast's as-of date, months covered, copies, band widening and sectors
- `world.json`: the world: kind (synthetic or real), generator, seed, counts
- `forecast.json`: the forecast's and its parameter fit's facts; each sector's fitted parameters
- `config.json`: the model configuration: fixed values and starting ranges
- `entities.json`: every entity (business): sector, tracked or representative, size, region, operator
- `entities/<entity>.json`: one entity: its hidden states over time (median, 90% band, truth) and observations
- `sectors/<sector>.json`: one sector: every quantity over time for its total, tracked and representative parts; official statistics against the model
- `observations.json`: every published reading, column by column (types, sources and subjects are lookup tables)
- `bundle.json`: the sector input bundle: drivers and official statistics as draws
- `quality.json`: the Evaluation numbers that need no ground truth
- `revisions.json`: forecasts against later estimates, series by series
- `accuracy.json`: errors against the true values (synthetic worlds only)
- `problems.json`: Current Problems (AI-written)
- `improvements.json`: Possible Improvements (AI-written)
- `testing.json`: Improvement Testing: every possible fix and what testing it found (AI-written)
- `datamodel.json`: the data model: tables, columns, keys and joins
